newsitem.title: USA: FedEx sees further int'l freight weakness.
newsitem.headline: FedEx sees further int'l freight weakness.

text.p: A weak international non-express airfreight market that helped dampen fiscal first-quarter earnings at Federal Express Corp will likely continue for the rest of the fiscal year, the company's chief financial officer said on Monday.
"I think you can expect to see lower yields for the rest of the fiscal year," said Alan B. Graf, Jr. in a conference call with reporters.
The company ealier on Monday posted first-quarter earnings of $1.08 per share, versus $1.33 per share in last year's first quarter.
Wall Street's consensus estimate for this year's quarter was $1.13, based on 10 estimates ranging from $0.90 to $1.32.

The company blamed the lower results partially on a weaker international non-express airfreight market. It said extremely aggressive pricing in that market, particularly in Asia, resulted in lower yields, which reduced revenues by $7 million compared with last year.
But Graf noted that the company's International Priority express segment showed strong growth this year over last year.
"We continue to think we have the right international strategy," he said.

Separately, Graf said Federal Express will record an unusual gain in the fiscal second quarter from the loss of a damaged aircraft that was taken out of service. He added that the gain will be offset partially by higher ownership costs.
He said higher maintenance expenses, higher jet fuel pricing and one less operating day also contributed to the company's overall lower earnings this year.
